claims.text: POL-NS-24 lets a rider cancel at no charge when the driver has not arrived by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes, and refunds any fee charged in full. The schedule on EV-TRIP-06055 is 05:30, so the deadline was 05:35:00; the trip record's own derived driver_deadline block records arrived_by_deadline = false, arrived_at is null, and no arrival event appears anywhere in the event list, while the cancellation is logged at 05:37:20 — after the deadline on any reading. The 5.00 SGD fee therefore falls to be refunded in full.

The GPS trace corroborates the non-arrival rather than curing it. The arrival derivation computed on EV-GPS-06055 reports corroborated = false and nearest_fix = null, so no fix places the driver at the pickup within the arrival window (arrival_radius_m 50, pickup_zone_class STANDARD, window_sec 120, per POL-NS-21); coverage is 100% with no gaps and max_gap_sec 30, so the absence of a corroborating fix is not a coverage artefact; and the trace's closing fixes at 05:36:00, 05:36:30 and 05:37:00 all report speed 0, the trace ending at 05:37:00 without any arrival recorded. On POL-NS-24 the driver had not arrived at the pickup when the rider cancelled.

The charge is a no-show fee, and its own trigger is absent on this record. POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD fee only where the driver cancels after the free wait, and POL-NS-21 fixes the start of that wait at the driver's arrival when he had not arrived by the scheduled time. On EV-TRIP-06055 the free_wait derivation returns starts_at = null, ends_at = null and cancelled_after_free_wait = null; the cancellation is logged as by the RIDER and no driver cancellation appears in the events at all. A fee whose precondition was never reached cannot stand on EV-FARE-06055, and the rider is entitled to the refund of it.

The driver's own messages give the time away. On EV-CHAT-06055 he wrote at 05:31:30 'Sorry ah a bit late, coming in 6-7 min', his own estimate placing arrival around 05:38 — past the 05:35:00 deadline — and at 05:36:30 he wrote 'Almost there' while EV-GPS-06055 shows no arrival had occurred. His counter-statement that he was 'only a few minutes late' is an admission of late arrival, and a driver late past the scheduled time plus five minutes is exactly what POL-NS-24 addresses.

The driver's answer — that he 'messaged and called her' — is true but beside the point. EV-TRIP-06055's contact_before_cancel derivation records one answered 35 s call at 05:32:10 and two messages, so the POL-NS-23 contact obligation was met; but POL-NS-23 conditions a no-show fee charged where the driver cancels, and it cannot cure a failure to arrive by the POL-NS-24 deadline. For the same reason the rider does not claim the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit POL-NS-24 reserves for a driver who also failed to attempt contact: the rider's claim is the refund of the fee, and nothing more.

Nothing in the record displaces the non-arrival finding. The only incomplete item is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06055-01, which is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; under POL-GEN-02(3) a missing artifact carries no fact, so it cannot be used to explain or excuse the missed deadline, and no clause of POLICY-NO-SHOW admits a traffic excuse to POL-NS-24's deadline in any event.

The record supports a final monetary ruling, not a referral upward. Both profiles carry fraud_flags = 0 (EV-RPROF-06055 for the rider, EV-DPROF-06055 for the driver), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 fraud band is not engaged, and the contested amount of 5.00 SGD is below the 10.00 SGD threshold at which the AI ruling is final. Every fact POL-NS-24 needs — the scheduled time, the cancellation time and the driver's non-arrival — is established on complete artifacts at weight 1.0, so POL-GEN-26 has no open question to escalate.

The remedy the record supports is precise: EV-FARE-06055 shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the whole contested amount is still live; POL-NS-24's refund is unqualified and no clause transfers a voided fee to the driver. Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is FULL_REFUND of the whole 5.00 SGD to the rider, with no driver compensation.

The rider's refund cannot rest on the driver's contact obligation.

The 5.00 SGD on the ledger is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 fixes, and the ledger reconciles to it end to end - policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_matches_policy true, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, payment_status CHARGED - so the record shows no amount defect in the charge for the rider to attack. Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 sends that same 5.00 SGD to the driver as compensation for time and fuel (DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00), and on POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION would at the least leave the charge standing, party-relative, exactly where the platform put it.

POL-NS-24's trigger is a failure to arrive at the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes, and this record's own arrival evidence does not deliver that finding. The trip record carries no arrival event (arrived_at null), and the derived arrival check accordingly returns arrived_at null and corroborated: false, with nearest_fix: null - the block reports that no arrival was corroborated, not a corroborated position at 05:35 that places the driver away from the pickup. The rider's 'more than 2 km away' is her own statement; no derived value in this record carries a distance from the pickup at any time. POL-GEN-26 names 'when the driver arrived' among the facts a rule may need and forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence: the open question belongs before a human reviewer with the 5.00 SGD held rather than refunded on an inference.

What the trace does show is a driver working the approach rather than abandoning it: 18 of 18 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps, a maximum gap of 30 s and every fix reporting 4-8 m accuracy (admissibility COMPLETE, weight 1.0), with the fixes moving at 17-35 km/h from 05:28:30 to 05:35:30 and the rider kept informed by two messages and an answered 35-second call. For the final three fixes, 05:36:00 to 05:37:00, the payload reports 0 km/h, and no artifact on the record explains that stop. The 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes is compensation for the driver's time and fuel on a trip already under way, sitting on the same five-minute clock POL-NS-21 sets; nothing in the record shows the driver had stopped working this trip.

The record carries no traffic-data artifact at all: EV-ADVIS-06055-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so I cite it as impaired, not as clean, and under POL-GEN-02(3) it carries no fact. The consequence is narrow but real: nothing on this record states the road conditions during the final minutes of the approach, so no account of them - the rider's or the driver's - can be corroborated or contradicted from it.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged on TRP-06055 (EV-FARE-06055, total_charged 5.00) is refunded in full to the rider.

WHY. The trip was scheduled for 05:30 (EV-TRIP-06055). Under POL-NS-24 (POLICY-NO-SHOW), if the driver has not arrived at the pickup by the scheduled time plus five minutes — 05:35 — the rider may cancel at no charge and any fee charged is refunded in full. The driver had not arrived by 05:35, and the rider cancelled at 05:37:20 (EV-TRIP-06055), after that deadline.

The finding rests on complete artifacts, each at weight 1.0. EV-TRIP-06055 carries no arrival event at all (arrived_at null; driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline false against the 05:35:00 deadline). EV-GPS-06055, the driver-device trace, is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and covers 05:28:30 to 05:37:00 with 18 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 30 s; no fix places the driver inside POL-NS-21's 50 m arrival radius (arrival_check.corroborated false, nearest_fix null) — the closest recorded approach is still about 2 km short, and the last three fixes, 05:36:00 to 05:37:00, sit stationary at 1.355117, 103.948502, roughly 2.3 km from the pickup at 1.3713, 103.962. EV-CHAT-06055, weight 1.0, records the driver's own words inside the window — 'Sorry ah a bit late, coming in 6-7 min' at 05:31:30 and 'Almost there' at 05:36:30 — and his statement that he was 'only a few minutes late' is an admission that he had not arrived by 05:35.

ANSWERING THE DRIVER'S POINTS. (1) It is true, under POL-NS-23, that the driver met the contact obligation: one answered 35 s in-app call at 05:32:10 and two chat messages, all before the cancellation. That obligation only conditions a no-show fee charged where the driver cancels; it does not cure a failure to arrive by the POL-NS-24 deadline and cannot make payable a fee that POL-NS-24 says is refunded. (2) The fee amount is correct under POL-NS-22 (5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy true, total_charged 5.00), but amount correctness is not entitlement: the free wait under POL-NS-21 never began, because the driver never arrived (starts_at null; ends_at null; cancelled_after_free_wait null), and the cancellation was logged as by the rider, so the precondition POL-NS-22 states for the fee — the driver cancelling after the free wait — was never met. (3) The POL-GEN-26 escalation argument is rejected: POL-GEN-26 applies where the evidence that would carry a needed fact is missing or impaired, and here the arrival question is answered by complete, weight-1.0 artifacts — a test that runs and finds no arrival has run. The stationary fixes at 05:36:00–05:37:00 are not an arrival and leave no open question for the deadline. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06055-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and POL-NS-24 admits no traffic excuse, so it neither explains the missed deadline nor leaves the arrival question open.

NO REFERRAL IS ADDED. The 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 does not apply because the driver did attempt contact. The POL-NS-22 fee-amount check does not fire because the fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee. POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not fire: the fee does not stand and the profile carries no such counter.

CONFIDENCE 0.92. The cap is 1.0, the minimum weight among the artifacts carrying the finding — EV-TRIP-06055, EV-GPS-06055 and EV-CHAT-06055, each 1.0. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final.

OUTCOME: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD to the rider; no driver compensation.

The driver therefore had not arrived by the deadline, so the rider was entitled to cancel at no charge and the fee of 5.00 SGD (EV-FARE-06055: total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, payment_status CHARGED) is returned in full. That obligation is a condition on a driver-initiated no-show, however; it does not cure a failure to arrive by the POL-NS-24 deadline, and it does not revive a fee whose free-wait trigger never occurred. For the same reason the driver's argument that the fee stands and should pass to him as compensation under POL-NS-22 fails: the fee's precondition is absent on this record. The suggestion that the non-arrival is merely uncorroborated and so must be escalated under POL-GEN-26 is not accepted — every artifact POL-NS-24 reads is complete at weight 1.0, the non-arrival is affirmatively established, and there is no open question to send up. Rider and driver: the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged on EV-FARE-06055 is refunded in full to the rider.

Governing clause: POL-NS-24 (driver no-show). The scheduled pickup was 05:30 (EV-TRIP-06055), so the deadline was 05:35:00. The driver had not arrived at the pickup by that time, nor by the rider's cancellation at 05:37:20.

The record establishes this on complete artifacts at weight 1.0:
- EV-TRIP-06055 records no arrival event (arrived_at null; derived driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline false), and logs the cancellation at 05:37:20 as RIDER_CANCELLED.
- EV-GPS-06055 is complete (18 of 18 fixes at 30 s, 100% coverage, max gap 30 s), and its arrival check finds no fix within the 50 m arrival radius of the pickup (nearest_fix null, corroborated false); the trace ends at 05:37:00 with the driver still short of the pickup. The absence of a corroborating fix is not a coverage artefact, so the driver's suggestion that the arrival block merely reports a missing reading, rather than a driver away from the pickup, is rejected.
- EV-CHAT-06055 carries the driver's own words: 'Sorry ah a bit late, coming in 6-7 min' at 05:31:30 (his own estimate placing arrival around 05:38, past the deadline) and 'Almost there' at 05:36:30. His counter-statement that he was 'only a few minutes late' concedes lateness.

The driver's point that he met his contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is accepted: EV-TRIP-06055 shows an answered 35-second in-app call at 05:32:10 and two messages before the cancellation, so the refund does not rest on POL-NS-23. But satisfying the contact obligation does not cure a failure to arrive by the POL-NS-24 deadline.

The driver's POL-GEN-26 escalation argument is rejected: escalation applies where a needed fact cannot be established, but the arrival fact is established by a complete trace, so there is no open question to hold.

The driver's POL-NS-22 claim for DRIVER_COMPENSATION is rejected: that fee attaches when the driver cancels after the free wait. Here the rider cancelled, the trip record's free_wait derivation returns null (the wait never started because the driver never arrived), and POL-NS-24 governs. Compensation to the driver follows only 'where the fee stands', and it does not stand.

No goodwill credit is added: POL-NS-24's extra 5.00 SGD credit applies only if the driver also failed to attempt contact, and he did attempt it (and the rider did not claim it).

No referral arises. The amount charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes (fee_matches_policy true, total_charged 5.00), so the POL-NS-22 amount referral is not triggered; the free wait was never reached; and the rider's profile carries no repeat no-show counter, so POL-NS-25 is not engaged.

POL-GEN-22: the contested value is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (both 0), so this ruling is final.

EV-ADVIS-06055-01 (traffic advisory) is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; under POL-GEN-02(3) it carries no fact, and no clause admits a traffic excuse to POL-NS-24's deadline.

Outcome: FULL_REFUND of the whole contested 5.00 SGD to the rider (EV-FARE-06055: total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, payment_status CHARGED); driver_compensation_sgd is null.

ruling.explanation:
Rider R-63263 booked TRP-06055 for a 05:30 pickup at Block 440, Pasir Ris Drive 6. Driver D-27956 was assigned at 05:28 and set off, but he never reached the pickup. The driver-device GPS trace (EV-GPS-06055, weight 1.0: 18 fixes at 30-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps, every fix reporting 4-8 m accuracy) shows him still working his way in and still roughly 2 km short of the pickup through its last fix at 05:37:00; the trip record (EV-TRIP-06055, weight 1.0) carries no arrival event at all and logs the rider's cancellation at 05:37:20. POL-NS-24 gives the rider the right to cancel at no charge where the driver has not arrived by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes -- 05:35:00 on this record -- and refunds any fee charged in full; the record's own driver_deadline derivation returns arrived_by_deadline = false. The 5.00 SGD charged on EV-FARE-06055 (payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is therefore returned in full.

The driver's points are answered. His contact obligation under POL-NS-23 was in fact met -- he messaged at 05:31:30 and 05:36:30 and placed an answered 35-second in-app call at 05:32:10, with contact_before_cancel.obligation_met = true -- but POL-NS-23 governs whether a no-show fee may be charged where the driver cancels, and it cannot cure a failure to arrive by the POL-NS-24 deadline. His argument that the record cannot establish the failure to arrive, so that POL-GEN-26 should escalate, does not hold: the GPS trace is complete and unimpaired and covers the whole deadline window (05:28:30-05:37:00), and its arrival check returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null, so the non-arrival is a finding the evidence carries, not a gap in it. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06055-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact under POL-GEN-02(3), and no no-show clause admits a traffic excuse to the POL-NS-24 deadline.

Because the driver did attempt contact, the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit POL-NS-24 reserves for a driver who also failed to contact does not arise. No referral fires either: the fee charged matches the 5.00 SGD policy fee for POL-NS-22, and the rider profile does not carry the POL-NS-25 counter in a way that triggers a repeat no-show flag, so nothing is added to the refund. Both profiles carry fraud_flags = 0 and the contested amount of 5.00 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so under POL-NS-26 this AI ruling is final. The rider is refunded the whole 5.00 SGD and the driver receives no compensation.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-24 lets a rider cancel at no charge when the driver has not arrived by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes, and refunds any fee charged in full. The schedule on EV-TRIP-06055 is 05:30, so the deadline was 05:35:00; the trip record's own derived driver_deadline block records arrived_by_deadline = false, arrived_at is null, and no arrival event appears anywhere in the event list, while the cancellation is logged at 05:37:20 — after the deadline on any reading. The 5.00 SGD fee therefore falls to be refunded in full.

The GPS trace corroborates the non-arrival rather than curing it. The arrival derivation computed on EV-GPS-06055 reports corroborated = false and nearest_fix = null, so no fix places the driver at the pickup within the arrival window (arrival_radius_m 50, pickup_zone_class STANDARD, window_sec 120, per POL-NS-21); coverage is 100% with no gaps and max_gap_sec 30, so the absence of a corroborating fix is not a coverage artefact; and the trace's closing fixes at 05:36:00, 05:36:30 and 05:37:00 all report speed 0, the trace ending at 05:37:00 without any arrival recorded. On POL-NS-24 the driver had not arrived at the pickup when the rider cancelled.

The charge is a no-show fee, and its own trigger is absent on this record. POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD fee only where the driver cancels after the free wait, and POL-NS-21 fixes the start of that wait at the driver's arrival when he had not arrived by the scheduled time. On EV-TRIP-06055 the free_wait derivation returns starts_at = null, ends_at = null and cancelled_after_free_wait = null; the cancellation is logged as by the RIDER and no driver cancellation appears in the events at all. A fee whose precondition was never reached cannot stand on EV-FARE-06055, and the rider is entitled to the refund of it.

The driver's own messages give the time away. On EV-CHAT-06055 he wrote at 05:31:30 'Sorry ah a bit late, coming in 6-7 min', his own estimate placing arrival around 05:38 — past the 05:35:00 deadline — and at 05:36:30 he wrote 'Almost there' while EV-GPS-06055 shows no arrival had occurred. His counter-statement that he was 'only a few minutes late' is an admission of late arrival, and a driver late past the scheduled time plus five minutes is exactly what POL-NS-24 addresses.

The driver's answer — that he 'messaged and called her' — is true but beside the point. EV-TRIP-06055's contact_before_cancel derivation records one answered 35 s call at 05:32:10 and two messages, so the POL-NS-23 contact obligation was met; but POL-NS-23 conditions a no-show fee charged where the driver cancels, and it cannot cure a failure to arrive by the POL-NS-24 deadline. For the same reason the rider does not claim the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit POL-NS-24 reserves for a driver who also failed to attempt contact: the rider's claim is the refund of the fee, and nothing more.

Nothing in the record displaces the non-arrival finding. The only incomplete item is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06055-01, which is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; under POL-GEN-02(3) a missing artifact carries no fact, so it cannot be used to explain or excuse the missed deadline, and no clause of POLICY-NO-SHOW admits a traffic excuse to POL-NS-24's deadline in any event.

The record supports a final monetary ruling, not a referral upward. Both profiles carry fraud_flags = 0 (EV-RPROF-06055 for the rider, EV-DPROF-06055 for the driver), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 fraud band is not engaged, and the contested amount of 5.00 SGD is below the 10.00 SGD threshold at which the AI ruling is final. Every fact POL-NS-24 needs — the scheduled time, the cancellation time and the driver's non-arrival — is established on complete artifacts at weight 1.0, so POL-GEN-26 has no open question to escalate.

The remedy the record supports is precise: EV-FARE-06055 shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the whole contested amount is still live; POL-NS-24's refund is unqualified and no clause transfers a voided fee to the driver. Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is FULL_REFUND of the whole 5.00 SGD to the rider, with no driver compensation.

The driver met the contact obligation POL-NS-23 imposes before any no-show: the chat log carries a driver message at 05:31:30 ('Sorry ah a bit late, coming in 6-7 min') and a second at 05:36:30 ('Almost there'), and the trip record carries an in-app call placed by the driver at 05:32:10 that was answered and ran 35 seconds - both limbs complete well before the 05:37:20 cancellation, with the derived contact_before_cancel block recording complete: true and obligation_met: true. The rider's refund cannot rest on the driver's contact obligation.

The 5.00 SGD on the ledger is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 fixes, and the ledger reconciles to it end to end - policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_matches_policy true, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, payment_status CHARGED - so the record shows no amount defect in the charge for the rider to attack. Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 sends that same 5.00 SGD to the driver as compensation for time and fuel (DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00), and on POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION would at the least leave the charge standing, party-relative, exactly where the platform put it.

POL-NS-24's trigger is a failure to arrive at the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes, and this record's own arrival evidence does not deliver that finding. The trip record carries no arrival event (arrived_at null), and the derived arrival check accordingly returns arrived_at null and corroborated: false, with nearest_fix: null - the block reports that no arrival was corroborated, not a corroborated position at 05:35 that places the driver away from the pickup. The rider's 'more than 2 km away' is her own statement; no derived value in this record carries a distance from the pickup at any time. POL-GEN-26 names 'when the driver arrived' among the facts a rule may need and forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence: the open question belongs before a human reviewer with the 5.00 SGD held rather than refunded on an inference.

What the trace does show is a driver working the approach rather than abandoning it: 18 of 18 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps, a maximum gap of 30 s and every fix reporting 4-8 m accuracy (admissibility COMPLETE, weight 1.0), with the fixes moving at 17-35 km/h from 05:28:30 to 05:35:30 and the rider kept informed by two messages and an answered 35-second call. For the final three fixes, 05:36:00 to 05:37:00, the payload reports 0 km/h, and no artifact on the record explains that stop. The 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes is compensation for the driver's time and fuel on a trip already under way, sitting on the same five-minute clock POL-NS-21 sets; nothing in the record shows the driver had stopped working this trip.

The record carries no traffic-data artifact at all: EV-ADVIS-06055-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so I cite it as impaired, not as clean, and under POL-GEN-02(3) it carries no fact. The consequence is narrow but real: nothing on this record states the road conditions during the final minutes of the approach, so no account of them - the rider's or the driver's - can be corroborated or contradicted from it.
